title: I clean an ice rink alone after closing. Someone's been skating under the ice.
story:
Scrape. Glide. Scrape. Glide. Someone was skating in the dark at the far end of the rink. But the ice was empty.

I'm the night guy at a small town rink. Last skate ends at ten, I flood the ice, and I'm alone until morning. The lost and found sits by my office door. Mostly single gloves. And one pair of white skates that nobody ever claimed.

When I hit the big lights, the sound stopped. But there were marks on the ice. Long curves, looping around and around. They weren't on top. They were underneath. Frozen in.

I told myself it was old lines showing through. So I drove the resurfacer over them twice. Fresh water, smooth as glass.

Ten minutes later, the scraping started again. Closer. Right below my feet.

I knelt and wiped the frost away with my sleeve. A face looked up at me through the ice. A woman, eyes open, hair drifting. She pressed one hand flat against the other side.

Then she knocked. Three soft taps, from under the ice. "Lace up," she whispered. "Skate with me."

I ran for the office door. The lost and found box was tipped over. The white skates were gone.

Behind me, a blade scraped tile.
premise: night worker at an ice rink hears skating with no one on the ice; a woman knocks from beneath the ice asking him to skate; the never-claimed white skates in lost and found are gone and she is behind him
theme: night shift at an ice rink
